synth.fraud_domain_gap: Beyond AIForge-Doc the fraud-domain space splits into three non-overlapping pieces, and the damage-photo intersection is empty. (a) DOCUMENT side is now covered: AIForge-Doc (2602.20569) does AI-inpainting tampering of numeric fields on real receipts/forms (CORD/WildReceipt/SROIE/XFUND) with pixel masks; DocForge-Bench and DocTamper/T-SROIE/'Find it again!' surround it. So the receipt/invoice half of claims fraud is addressed (months old, not deeply). (b) LOCALIZED-EDIT DETECTION METHODOLOGY exists and is mature: DiffSeg30k (2511.19111), COCO-Inpaint (2504.18361), TGIF2 (2603.28613), INP-X (2602.00192), LocalizedDeepfakes (2512.16688), and (if real) LocateEdit-Bench/FragFake — all provide masks and/or instruction-editor coverage including the exact frontier fills of interest (Firefly, Flux.1-Fill, Gemini). But every one uses generic COCO/OmniEdit object edits with ZERO damage/insurance semantics. (c) DAMAGE-VISION side exists but only for ASSESSMENT, never forgery: CarDD (4,000 real car-damage photos, pixel masks, built to Ping An insurance-claim standards, 6 classes dent/scratch/crack/glass/lamp/tire), VehiDE (13,945 insurance-framed damaged-car photos), xBD (satellite building damage), MVTec AD (studio surface defects). PRECISE GAP: there is NO public benchmark or paper sitting at the intersection {authentic property/auto/hotel physical-damage photo + frontier instruction-edited ADDED damage (dent/crack/scratch/water-stain/mold/fire) + per-pixel forgery ground-truth mask + detector evaluation}. What is MISSING specifically: (1) no damage-domain detection benchmark at all; (2) no per-pixel evaluation of the named frontier editors (gpt-image, Gemini/Nano-Banana, Firefly, Flux.1-Fill) on the damage-synthesis task; (3) property/hotel/water-mold-fire damage has NO mask-annotated authentic base comparable to CarDD (auto is the only well-covered sub-domain — property/hotel is a second, deeper gap); (4) no systematic edit-size x blending/harmonization sweep and no laundering (JPEG re-compress / screenshot / messenger re-upload / print-scan) robustness sweep in ANY domain; (5) no broad commercial-API panel (Hive/Sightengine/Verisk/VAARHAFT) tested on small localized edits. The convergence of (frontier capability + documented active fraud + zero damage-domain detection benchmark) is the genuine, narrow opening.
recommended_real_bases: CarDD (4,000 real high-res car-damage photos; 9,000+ instances; 6 fine-grained classes; pixel-level instance masks; built to Ping An insurance-claim standards by annotators incl. 5 insurance experts) — the single strongest authentic base; its damage masks double as ready-made edit-region priors. License form required; non-commercial; bound by Flickr/Shutterstock terms (so original consumer EXIF is generally stripped).

VehiDE (13,945 real damaged-car photos; 32,000+ instances; ~8 insurance-aligned categories + non-damage; Kaggle) — adds scale and explicit insurance pricing-rule annotation; confirm the live Kaggle license before use.

Roboflow Universe / Kaggle auto-damage sets (CAPSTONE, Car Damage Assessment 3,772, Car Damage V5, COCO Car Damage, severity sets) — smartphone/claim-style diversity to complement CarDD/VehiDE; per-dataset licenses vary (often CC BY 4.0); verify each.

Receipt/form bases reused by AIForge-Doc: CORD, WildReceipt, SROIE, XFUND (+ T-SROIE / 'Find it again!') — the authentic base for the document half; standard research OCR corpora with PII-like fields (use under research license, scrub PII).

Provenance-bearing real-camera bases (RAISE-RAW, SIDD, VISION, Dresden, Forchheim, MIT-Adobe FiveK) — REQUIRED if you want to study the metadata/PRNU axis honestly, because CarDD/VehiDE lack genuine consumer-camera EXIF/RAW; use these as the 'real provenance' control or as a re-capture pipeline reference.

Established localized-edit/forgery benchmarks as the DETECTION-SIDE references to stress-test and to borrow methodology from: COCO-Inpaint (2504.18361), TGIF/TGIF2 (2407.11566 / 2603.28613, source CC-BY-4.0 COCO), DiffSeg30k (2511.19111), INP-X (2602.00192), AutoSplice, CocoGlide, IMD2020, DEFACTO, CASIA/NIST16 — public, mask-bearing, and exactly the detectors-to-break.

GAP NOTE: no public hotel-room/furniture or water-mold-fire property-damage dataset of meaningful scale exists (only ~116-image Roboflow furniture-defect sets and a hosted Nyckel classifier). xBD (satellite) and MVTec (studio) are poor proxies for ground-level claim photos. Property/hotel imagery would have to be commissioned, licensed, or re-captured — this is the binding data constraint for going beyond auto.
synth.defender_model: A realistic 2026 claim-photo authenticity pipeline is LAYERED and leans on cheap/robust database and metadata signals, not a pixel-perfect inpainting localizer. Model the defender as: (1) REUSE/DUPLICATE detection — perceptual hashing (pHash) + visual embeddings against the carrier's own archive and the industry-shared cross-carrier database (Verisk ClaimSearch Image Matching covering >95% of the industry; VAARHAFT federated cross-insurance duplicate check; Shift/FRISS reused-media), plus reverse-image search (TinEye/Yandex/Google) for stock/web scrapes. This is the HIGHEST-YIELD, most reliable layer and the one with documented catches (Segway scheme matched across 6 carriers; 768K-image study found 1,967 dups). (2) METADATA/EXIF consistency — capture timestamp/timezone/GPS/device vs the claim narrative, plus missing-metadata/screenshot flags (insurers therefore demand ORIGINAL files). Cheap, widely used, treated as a SOFT signal because trivially spoofable/strippable. (3) CLASSIC PIXEL FORENSICS — Error Level Analysis, noise/clone/double-JPEG checks, PRNU/noise-pattern (a single image with >1 camera noise signature implies compositing); Zurich SIU credits metadata anomalies + ELA for catching fake car images. (4) NEWER GenAI/deepfake CLASSIFIER — a probabilistic 'manipulated?' score (Verisk deepfake module described as beta/in-development; VAARHAFT, TruthScan, Inaza, UVeye, Inspektlabs) — the least battle-tested layer against subtle inpainting. (5) ENTITY/NETWORK ANALYTICS (Quantexa at Zurich) linking claims/people/devices. (6) CAPTURE-TIME PROVENANCE — Truepic Lens SDK / Serelay in-app signed capture, C2PA Content Credentials — the STRONGEST single control, but only present where the insurer forces in-app capture (virtual inspections), NOT for typical inbound claimant phone photos. WHY THE THREAT EVADES IT (model this as the attack surface): a fresh, unique, genuinely-captured phone JPEG with one small AI-added dent passes (1) [not a duplicate], passes (2) [base capture is real, EXIF stays consistent, editors can preserve/regenerate plausible EXIF], often passes (3) [modern diffusion re-harmonizes noise; ELA weak], sits below (4)'s threshold [<5% mask ~chance per LocalizedDeepfakes; 91->55% per INP-X], and defeats (6) [no manifest on consumer JPEG; absence proves nothing; C2PA strippable/re-signable]. The only durable passive signal is PRNU (edited region loses the sensor fingerprint) but it needs ~100-200 reference images from the SAME phone, fails in dark/saturated/textured regions where damage lives, and degrades under recompression — so it is an 'only-if-phone-available' control, not a default. Net defender to beat: dedup + EXIF + ELA + a probabilistic GenAI classifier; capture-time provenance and PRNU are strong but usually absent.
synth.frontier_editor_feasibility: FEASIBLE for adding damage; PARTIALLY studied for detection but never in the damage domain. CAPABILITY: frontier instruction editors are documented to do exactly fine localized natural-language edits with surrounding-context consistency, and they already power adjacent benchmarks — Gemini 2.5 Flash Image (Nano-Banana) and Ideogram v2 do the numeric-field inpainting in AIForge-Doc; Adobe Firefly and Flux.1[Fill] do object inpainting in TGIF2; Qwen-Image-Edit/Flux-Kontext/Step1X/BAGEL drive LocateEdit-Bench (if real); gpt-image is the same model class. Adding a dent/scratch/crack/water-stain/mold/scorch to an authentic damage photo is a strictly easier, more textural local edit than legible numeric-field synthesis, so it is plausibly within reach for these editors with localized inpainting. The real cracked-bumper Allianz/LV= case (AI-added bumper crack on a social-media van photo, >£1,000 claim) is field evidence the capability already exists in the wild. QUALITY CAVEAT: expect a non-trivial reject rate (AIForge-Doc rejected 5 of 7 tools for illegible/incorrect output; damage is more forgiving on legibility but harder on physical plausibility — shadow direction, reflection, material consistency, edge harmonization, scale). DETECTION-IS-STUDIED status: localized-edit DETECTION of these exact editors IS studied on generic content (TGIF2 shows FLUX.1 hardest to detect and generative-SR destroys forensic traces; DiffSeg30k/COCO-Inpaint/INP-X/LocalizedDeepfakes all evaluate detectors on diffusion inpainting and show collapse on small edits), but NO study evaluates detection of frontier-editor DAMAGE synthesis on real damage photos with per-pixel ground truth. So: editors can almost certainly do it; detectors are known to fail on small localized diffusion edits generically; the damage-specific detection question is genuinely open and is the project's contribution surface.
synth.feasibility_for_fraud_corpus: FEASIBLE and relatively cheap for the AUTO sub-domain; expensive/blocked for property/hotel. BUILD RECIPE (auto): take CarDD + VehiDE + Roboflow auto sets as authentic bases; use their existing damage masks (or fresh masks) as edit-region priors; generate localized added-damage edits via a small panel of frontier editors (e.g., Gemini 2.5 Flash Image, Flux.1-Fill, Firefly, gpt-image) in BOTH spliced (preserve unmasked real pixels, INP-X/SP style) and fully-regenerated modes; keep DocTamper-compatible per-pixel masks. Add a deliberate edit-SIZE x BLENDING sweep and a LAUNDERING sweep (JPEG QF, resize, screenshot, messenger re-upload, optional generative-SR) — these are precisely the axes ALL verified papers skipped, so they are where the marginal novelty sits. EFFORT/COST: a CarDD-scale corpus (a few thousand to ~10-30k edited images across 4 editors x 2 modes x size/blend/laundering grid) is a modest API/compute spend (low-thousands USD of editor-API calls) plus the dominant cost = quality filtering and mask QA (manual or VLM-assisted accept/reject, given the expected reject rate). Detector eval is cheap: run released weights of TruFor, DocTamper, CAT-Net, IML-ViT, SegFormer, DINOv3, plus 1-2 commercial APIs if budget allows. FEASIBILITY BLOCKERS: (1) PROPERTY/HOTEL/water-mold-fire has no public mask-annotated base — covering it requires commissioning/licensing/re-capturing imagery, a real time-and-money cost that likely pushes the first paper to AUTO-ONLY (+ receipts via AIForge-Doc bases). (2) CarDD/Shutterstock licensing forbids redistributing base images and the bases lack genuine consumer EXIF, so a metadata/PRNU axis needs provenance-bearing bases (RAISE/SIDD/VISION) or a re-capture step. (3) Commercial-API detector access (Hive/Sightengine/Verisk/VAARHAFT) is paywalled/gated — partial coverage is realistic, full panel is not. Overall: a gated AUTO+receipt corpus is clearly buildable in a few weeks at low cost; the science is real but the per-component novelty is thin, so value depends on the size/blend/laundering/commercial-API axes plus the domain-shift evidence, not on the corpus existing per se.
synth.ethics_gating_plan: Strictly defensive red-team framing; outputs must not become an evasion playbook. Concrete gates: (1) BASE DATA — use only licensed/public bases (CarDD via signed form, VehiDE/Roboflow per their licenses, CORD/SROIE/WildReceipt/XFUND research-only); NEVER scrape real insurer claim images or victims'/claimants' social-media property photos (the exact fraud vector); for receipts use de-identified or synthetic-PII versions. Respect non-redistribution (CarDD/Shutterstock, xBD CC BY-NC-SA, MVTec non-commercial). (2) PII — claim/damage photos carry faces, plates, addresses, GPS; scrub/redact, strip/avoid retaining EXIF-GPS, drop re-identifiable content; note CORD already withholds 10k images for PII. (3) ARTIFACT RELEASE — release ONLY aggregate detector catch/miss metrics and (optionally) GATED access to edited images under a research agreement; do NOT publicly release the edited images as scrapeable files, the masks-as-templates, the exact per-editor prompts, the size/blend parameters that evade a named detector, or any recapture/metadata-washing trick. Report capability gaps at the level of DETECTOR FAMILIES and THREAT CLASSES (as INP-X/LocalizedDeepfakes/AIForge-Doc do), never as a tuned recipe against a named vendor. (4) LABELING — watermark/label every AI-edited sample as synthetic (and consider C2PA labeling) to prevent leakage into real claims or training sets. (5) COORDINATED DISCLOSURE — share specific blind-spot findings with affected detector vendors/insurers (Verisk, Shift, VAARHAFT, Truepic) before public release, mirroring security norms. (6) LEGAL/FRAMING — state plainly that fabricating claims is a crime (e.g., NY Penal Law 176, Insurance Law 405(a); policy concealment/forfeiture clauses); keep the public-interest justification (FRE 901/707, liar's dividend) front and center. (7) MODEL the defenders (C2PA/Truepic/SynthID/Verisk) as black boxes reporting catch/miss rates, not as bypass instructions. (8) CONSENT — even defensively, editing real people's property raises consent issues; prefer consent-clean or commissioned bases.
synth.recommended_minimum_viable_paper: Title direction: 'Can detectors catch a fabricated dent? A damage-domain stress test of localized AI-edit detection on authentic auto-claim photos.' SCOPE the MVP to AUTO damage + receipts (defer property/hotel to future work, given no public base). DELIVERABLES that are genuinely new vs the verified literature: (1) FIRST damage-domain localized-edit detection benchmark — CarDD/VehiDE authentic bases + frontier-editor added-damage (Gemini/Flux.1-Fill/Firefly/gpt-image) in spliced + fully-regenerated modes, with per-pixel masks (the empty intersection). (2) The TWO axes every verified paper skipped: a parametric edit-SIZE x BLENDING/harmonization sweep, and a LAUNDERING robustness sweep (JPEG/resize/screenshot/messenger re-upload/generative-SR). (3) DOMAIN-SHIFT quantification: take detectors that 'work' on generic inpainting (COCO-Inpaint/TGIF2/INP-X numbers) and show how much further they drop on damage content and small damage edits — i.e., reproduce the INP-X 91->55 / LocalizedDeepfakes <5%-mask-~chance / AIForge-Doc 0.98->0.563 collapse but in the damage domain. (4) A BROADER detector panel than any single prior paper: open weights (TruFor, DocTamper, CAT-Net, IML-ViT, SegFormer, DINOv3) PLUS at least one commercial API (Hive/Sightengine/VAARHAFT) — INP-X had only Hive+Sightengine, AIForge-Doc had none. (5) DEFENDER-STACK realism: report not just classifier AUC but how the layered defender (dedup/EXIF/ELA/provenance) fares — show the small-edit case slips every layer. HONEST NOVELTY POSITIONING: frame as 'domain transfer + missing robustness axes + realistic defender,' NOT as a new method — the method/methodology already exists (DiffSeg30k/COCO-Inpaint/LocateEdit-Bench), so the contribution is the damage corpus, the size/blend/laundering sweeps, the commercial-API panel, and the defender-stack evaluation.
